lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernanda Bassani Rubio | Lesson 4 -- Last Quarter in Numbers
lesson.grammar_point: past simple regular verbs affirmative and negative

listenings.text: Good morning, everyone. Let me start with the numbers for the third quarter. Total sales increased by eight percent. That is good. In Brazil, we reached ninety-six percent of the target. In Argentina, we reached ninety percent. Together, that is ninety-four percent. So we didn't reach the target, but we are close. The main problem was August: prices dropped, and two customers delayed their orders. The good news is our market share. It increased from eighteen to twenty percent. And we signed one new contract. Fernanda, thank you for that. Now, questions?

Hi, I am Giulia, and I work with car makers in Italy. My quarter was not easy. In July, everything started well. We signed two small contracts, and sales increased. But in August, many factories in Italy closed for the summer holidays, so orders dropped a lot. In September, we worked very hard and we visited six customers. In the end, we reached one hundred and two percent of the target. I was very happy. What did I learn? I learned to plan August in June.

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: to get to a number or a goal
when something becomes bigger over time
to go down, to become smaller
a written agreement between two companies
a period of three months in the business year
to go up, to become bigger
the part of all sales in a market that one company has
a number that a team wants to reach

paras: Dear team, the third quarter ended on September 30, and I want to thank you for your work. First, the good news. Sales increased by eight percent compared with the second quarter. Our growth came mainly from adhesives for electric cars. We also signed a new contract with a car maker in Argentina, and our market share increased to twenty percent.

Now the difficult part. We didn't reach our sales target. We reached ninety-four percent of it. In August, prices dropped in the market, and two customers delayed their orders. The team worked very hard in September, but we didn't close the gap.

What did we learn? Our customers liked the new samples, and they asked for more technical visits. For the fourth quarter, we want to keep the growth and reach the target. Please send me your forecast by October 10. Best regards, Mark Evans, Regional Director.
